priority.when: For all git and gh CLI operations
priority.why: Git commands provide the historical context needed for intelligent resolution

priority.when: To examine conflicted files and understand the conflict structure
priority.why: Need to see the actual conflict markers and code

priority.when: To resolve conflicts by applying a focused patch
priority.why: Preserves exact context while replacing conflicted sections

best_practices.practice: Always use gh CLI for GitHub operations instead of MCP tools
Chain git commands with && for efficiency

command.purpose: Rebase onto main to reveal conflicts

best_practices.practice: Read the entire conflicted file first to understand structure
Note line numbers of conflict markers for precise editing
Identify the pattern of conflicts (multiple vs single)

conflict_parsing.marker: <<<<<<< HEAD - Start of current branch changes

tool.name: apply_patch

best_practices.practice: Read the file immediately before editing
Replace the complete conflict block, including marker lines
Include enough unchanged context in update hunks
Resolve one conflict block per patch when necessary

tool.name: apply_patch

best_practices.practice: Use when an exact conflict block has been read
Include all conflict marker lines in the patch hunk

tool.example:
apply_patch arguments:
{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: src/config.ts
@@
-<<<<<<< HEAD
-old configuration
-=======
-new configuration
->>>>>>> branch
+const config = {
+  // Merged settings from both branches
+}
*** End Patch"
}

sequence.step: run_command - Get PR info with gh CLI
run_command - Checkout PR with gh pr checkout --force
run_command - Check for conflicts with git status
run_command - Git blame on conflict regions
run_command - Continue rebase with git rebase --continue

scenario.name: no_conflicts_after_rebase
scenario.approach: Inform user that PR can be merged without conflicts No resolution needed

scenario.name: rebase_in_progress
scenario.description: A rebase is already in progress
scenario.approach: Check status with git status Either continue existing rebase or abort with git rebase --abort

scenario.name: malformed_conflicts
scenario.description: Conflict markers are incomplete or nested
scenario.approach: Inspect the complete block manually, then use apply_patch with exact content from the latest read_file result.

scenario.name: binary_conflicts
scenario.description: Binary files cannot be merged automatically
scenario.approach: Identify which version to keep based on PR intent Use git checkout --theirs or --ours

scenario.name: escaped_markers
scenario.description: Code contains literal conflict marker strings
scenario.approach: Include literal marker strings in the patch hunk and verify the result with read_file afterwards.
